Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: Smart card (contactless polycarbonate) enables on-card and offline authentication since 2018 (Semlex). Online/digital authentication (eKYC/ABIS verification) not yet operational; World Bank diagnostic states 'Absent; no fully operational eKYC/ABIS verification across systems'. Strategy proposes online authentication via identity bus. Card-based offline auth only.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025 establishes individual rights to access, rectify, erase, and port own data. Controllers required to respond within one month. No operational self-service portal for individuals to view their ID system data confirmed; legal right established under new Act.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: National ID card used for manual KYC in banking and telecoms under AML/CTF Act 2012. No electronic KYC (eKYC) platform operational; World Bank diagnostic: 'No eKYC; reliance on paper IDs causes frustration, AML issues'. Strategy proposes CKYC and unified eKYC framework. Smile ID third-party verification service supports remote ID document verification commercially.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Comments: DIDS strategy proposes judicial orders required for security services/police access to ID data. Personal Data Protection Act 2025 includes enforcement by Information Commission with investigative powers; legal pathways for complaints established. No specific court-based ongoing oversight mechanism for national ID system found.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: eCRVS (HERA software, 2022/2023) operational with 1.2M records. MOU signed March 2024 between ID and eCRVS systems for NIN harmonization. UAT for eCRVS-eID integration completed April 2025; health insurance cards link CRVS NIN with NHIS. Integration underway but different NIN structures remain a challenge. World Bank WARDIP project (P173287) supporting deployment.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025 establishes data sharing rules (purpose limitation, data minimisation, adequacy for cross-border transfers). DIDS strategy proposes limited data collection/access with consent, interoperability via open standards. No specific operational ID data sharing framework yet; rules exist in DPA law.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act enacted in 2025 (approved by National Assembly September 2025, reviewed Dec 2025). First comprehensive data protection legislation. Covers biometric data, data subject rights, breach notification, DPIAs. Ends long-standing gap since only constitutional privacy right existed previously.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025 designates the Information Commission (established under Access to Information Act 2021) as regulatory authority with enforcement powers: investigate complaints, enter/search premises with warrants, impose administrative sanctions and fines, issue enforcement notices. Dual mandate Commission (access to information + data protection).

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: National ID card accepted as legal proof of identity; citizens over 18 legally required to carry it. ID used as breeder document for services (banking, telecoms KYC per AML Act 2012). DIDS strategy proposes formal legal proof status for digital ID for eKYC/financial transactions.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: National Registration Act covers national ID card issuance. Immigration Act (1965) being updated via draft Immigration Bill (2023). Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act enacted 2025. Strategy recommends comprehensive DIDS law (not yet enacted). World Bank diagnostic identifies gaps: no cyber framework, no cross-border data transfer rules, no digital ID-specific statute.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Ministry of Interior (Dept of Immigration) owns National ID system. Jan 2026 PPP: 8-year build-cooperate-transfer contract with Margins ID Group; private partner finances and operates system, revenue shared 30/70 in favour of private partner, assets transferred to government at end. PPP maintenance model with government oversight.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Ministry of Finance was part of the technical procurement team for the 2026 PPP contract with Margins ID Group (alongside Interior, Justice, Digital Economy, GICTA). Revenue sharing (30/70) and asset transfer terms structured. No evidence of ongoing systematic MoF operational oversight of digital ID beyond contract approval.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: 8-year PPP with Margins ID Group (signed Jan 2026): private partner finances and operates system, 30/70 revenue share. Strategy total cost USD 22.24M (donor investment + government recurring). DIDS strategy explicitly calls for sustainable financing via PPP and donor resources. World Bank WARDIP and World Bank ID diagnostics also provide support. Medium-term sustainability secured via PPP.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Full biometric collection operational since 2009 (GAMBIS/Innovatrics). 2018 Semlex system collects 10 fingerprints and digital photo, stored in ABIS. eCRVS (2022/2023) also uses biometrics for deduplication. Biometric data for driving licences also linked to national ID system.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Gambia has a biometric national ID card (contactless smart card) operational since 2018 (Semlex system). National Digital ID Strategy 2023-2028 validated May 2024. 8-year PPP contract signed Jan 2026 with Margins ID Group for full National Identity Management System upgrade. No operational online/digital authentication platform yet; system is in transition to full digital ID.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Fragmented databases across ministries; no unified interoperable system. MOU signed March 2024 between Immigration (ID) and Health (eCRVS) for NIN harmonization. UAT for eCRVS-eID integration completed April 2025 for health cards. Identity bus proposed but not yet operational. Limited interoperability achieved.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National ID card used as primary KYC document for banking, insurance, money remittances under AML/CTF Act 2012. Voter ID also accepted as KYC tool. No electronic ID-bank integration (eKYC). DIDS strategy lists banks as key ecosystem partners; 'banks in Gambia are also envisaged to leverage authentication services of National Digital ID for KYC'. Current use: manual ID presentation.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: National ID card: 450 Dalasi (~USD 6.63) for first issuance, replacement, and renewal - same cost for all including vulnerable groups. No fee waivers. Birth certificate free within 30-90 days. World Bank diagnostic flags cost as barrier especially for vulnerable groups. Fee-based but not prohibitively high.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Gambia is one of 6 ECOWAS states (of 15) that has deployed the ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card (ENBIC) for regional free movement. Gambian biometric ID card noted as acceptable in most ECOWAS countries. ECOWAS Commission sensitized Gambia Immigration on ENBIC in 2023. Jan 2026 PPP will produce ICAO-compliant e-identity cards. Regional recognition via ECOWAS framework.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: National ID card: Gambian citizens 18 and above. DIDS strategy proposes biometric capture from age 5 (initial) and permanent profile at 18. eCRVS registers at birth. Current operational national ID system eligibility: 18+.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: DIDS strategy explicitly proposes voluntary enrollment: 'user choice on whether to enrol or to use the Unique ID (i.e., voluntary rather than compulsory enrolment)'. While citizens over 18 are legally required to carry an ID card, enrollment in the digital ID system is proposed as voluntary.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: eCRVS (2022) linked to National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS): health insurance cards issued using CRVS NIN, QR-enabled. HMIS uses eCRVS NIN to reduce duplicate patient records. 258 health facilities and 79 civil registration offices linked. Mass registration 2022-2023 issued health insurance cards to 1.2M+ individuals. Operational linkage between CRVS-based ID and healthcare.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Resident Permit cards issued separately for ECOWAS nationals and other foreign residents (12-digit NIN, renewed yearly). Jan 2026 PPP contract: Margins ID Group to produce residential permits for both ECOWAS and non-ECOWAS nationals. eCRVS health insurance cards available to all residents. Non-nationals eligible for separate credential; not same national ID.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: DIDS strategy proposes privacy/security by design, internal security/privacy audits, Service Provider compliance audits, ISO 29115 Level of Assurance standards. Personal Data Protection Act 2025 requires DPIAs for high-risk processing. No published independent security audit of national ID system found. World Bank ID diagnostic (2025) conducted systems review. Security review mechanisms proposed in law/strategy.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: PURA regulates SIM registration; ID document required for SIM registration. World Bank diagnostic: 'PURA SIM DB: No eID authentication; duplication/fraud issues. No validation of mobile numbers.' DIDS strategy: telecom companies are key ecosystem partners for eKYC. No confirmed electronic integration between national ID ABIS and PURA SIM registration database.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: GamSIR (Gambia Social Registry) covers 40 of 43 districts; 6 social protection programs use it; 1,039,043 beneficiaries. World Bank diagnostic: 'No foundational ID link' between GamSIR and national ID system. Social Security & Housing Finance has own 7-digit ID, no integration. Barcodes/QR codes used for beneficiary identification in cash transfers, not linked to national ID.
